doc_name: Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Songs of All Time
text: "The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time" is a recurring song ranking created by the American magazine Rolling Stone, based on weighted votes from selected musicians, critics, and industry figures. The first edition was published in December 2004 in Rolling Stone's special issue number 963, a year after the publication of "The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time." In 2010, Rolling Stone released a revised version that incorporated the original list and a later survey of songs released up to the early 2000s. A further updated edition appeared in 2021, featuring more than half the entries not present in either the 2004 or 2010 lists; this version was based on a new survey and did not include the data from prior surveys. The 2021 list was compiled from over 250 artists, musicians, producers, critics, journalists, and industry figures, each submitting a ranked list of their top 50 songs, which Rolling Stone then aggregated. In 2024, a revised version was published, including songs from the 2020s. In May 2010, Rolling Stone released a digital update for iPod and iPad, which included 26 new songs—25 from the 2000s and one, "Juicy" by The Notorious B.I.G., released in 1994. The top 25 songs remained unchanged, but many lower-ranked songs experienced shifts due to the addition of new entries, with Gnarls Barkley's "Crazy" reaching number 100 as the highest-ranked new song. The distribution of songs by decade in the 2010 update is: 11 songs from the 2010s, 7 from the 2000s, 6 from the 1990s, 5 from the 1980s, 4 from the 1970s, 3 from the 1960s, 2 from the 1950s, and no songs from the 1940s or earlier.
